recentItems.title: David Byrne: ‘You don't have to be like everyone else’
recentItems.description:
David Byrne is one of the most influential figures in modern music. As the frontman of Talking Heads, he helped create songs including ‘Psycho Killer’, ‘Once in a Lifetime’ and ‘Burning Down the House’, before building a career as a solo musician, writer and filmmaker. 

His new book, 'Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up', explores why some artists, inventions and ideas are forgotten before being rediscovered.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

In this episode of Ways to Change the World, Byrne talks to Krishnan Guru-Murthy about why we often assume the present is better than the past, and how forgotten ideas can offer new answers to modern problems. 

Byrne also reflects on neurodiversity, the making of Psycho Killer, creativity and collaboration, and whether the internet and AI will make it easier to rediscover ideas that have been lost.

recentItems.title: SPY WARS: can Europe’s spooks handle ‘EXPLOSION’ in Russian spy attacks?
recentItems.description:
In the last few days a former German spy chief has been accused of selling state secrets, a British navy sailor has been charged with espionage and now two Latvians have been picked up near a British air base in Cambridgeshire - not to mention the mysterious goings on at RAF Fairford.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Meanwhile, in Germany, the former head of the foreign intelligence service August Hanning has been arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power. 

Hanning denies the allegations. His lawyer says that while he was in possession of confidential documents, he did not pass them on to foreign powers or receive payment for doing so, and says his client is being wrongfully prosecuted.

So are Western intelligence agencies facing a growing threat? Or was it ever thus? 

In this episode of the Fourcast Indicators, Krishnan Guru Murthy and Mark Urban are joined by former national security adviser Sir Mark Lyall Grant.

recentItems.title: Search warrants on Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s homes were unlawful
recentItems.description:
It was a rare moment of victory for Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, as a court confirmed that the search warrant used on two of his homes as Thames Valley Police investigate him for alleged misconduct in public office were unlawful.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The raids were carried out after Andrew was arrested in February.

The material seized will not yet be handed back, as the police seek to get retrospective permission to retain it. Further court hearings will decide that.

The stakes are very high. If they fail, it could all be handed back with little hope of another chance

recentItems.title: Can the UK protect itself from growing security threats?
recentItems.description:
A 24-year-old Royal Navy sailor is accused of plotting to leak information to Russia, as the UK's national security is a growing focus both at home and on the international stage. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

It comes as two Latvians were arrested after they were found inside the base perimeter of RAF Molesworth.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has been in Germany, discussing a partnership to guard against future threats, while the foreign secretary Ed Miliband was in Ukraine announcing new sanctions on Russian military supply chains.
